correctness.summary: For a clique Q=K_q and two remaining vertices x,y, the four Venn-cell sizes of N_Q(x) and N_Q(y) determine all distances and all Szeged edge contributions. Direct summation gives the three exact formulas according to whether xy is present and whether the common-neighbor cell is empty. Combining those formulas with the exact 2-connectivity criterion reduces eta(G)=2n to elementary nonnegative integer equations. For q=n-2>=8, the only solutions are the Zhang-Li family for every q and, when q=8, one additional isomorphism type with clique-neighborhood sizes 1 and 2 sharing their unique common neighbor. Definition-level computation agrees with all formulas and the connectivity criterion for q<=10 and with the classification for every parameter type through q=40.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The accessible current full text of Zhang-Li, arXiv:2609.20025v1, proves eta(G)>=2n, poses classification of equality as an explicit open problem, and gives one equality construction for every n>=10, but does not give the (n-2)-clique slice or the exact two-vertex-extension formulas. The accessible Bonamy-Knor-Luzar-Pinlou-Skrekovski primary preprint arXiv:1602.05184 proves and classifies equality in the older 2n-6 bound, not the present theorem. Targeted searches for Szeged-Wiener equality combined with clique number, near-complete graphs, (n-2)-cliques, two-vertex clique extensions, and eta(G)=2n found no equivalent result. No specific inaccessible paper was identified as a likely source of prior coverage; unindexed or differently-termed literature remains a residual risk.

value.summary: The result solves the newly posed eta(G)=2n equality problem completely in the natural high-clique regime. It proves uniqueness of the source construction for every n>=11, identifies the unique order-10 exception, and supplies exact closed formulas for the Szeged-Wiener gap of every connected graph obtained by adjoining two vertices to a clique.

limitations: The equality classification is restricted to graphs containing an (n-2)-clique; equality graphs with smaller clique number are not classified.
The newest source notes that its construction is not necessary in general, so further equality types may occur outside this regime.
Finite exhaustive verification supports but does not replace the symbolic proof.
No specific inaccessible paper was identified as a likely source of prior coverage, but unindexed recent work or substantially different terminology remains a residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
